dedupe_keys.name: space industry technical standards compendium us office of space commerce

description: The Space Industry Technical Standards Compendium is a table of technical standards, specifications, guidance documents and programme publications relevant to commercial space activities. For each entry it gives the developer and designation, the title, the publication date, the status (published, in development or out of print), a category and whether the document is free or requires a fee. Its roughly 540 rows cover standards bodies and agencies such as CCSDS, SAE, ISO, ASTM, AIAA, NASA and NIST, with categories led by space data exchange, risk management, test, debris mitigation, launch, human space safety, safety and operations, plus smaller groups on cybersecurity, end of mission, space sustainability and debris awareness. It was compiled by the Office of Space Commerce and published as a 15-page PDF in June 2024, free to download from the office's website; the underlying standards keep their own terms and many need purchase. Caveats: it is a US-compiled snapshot that lists documents without summarising their content, and statuses will date. It helps modellers find the standards that set design margins, debris mitigation, space situational awareness data exchange and operations practice for space infrastructure, and supports resilience and hazard exposure assumptions; a related record is ISO TR 23689 on space weather information for operations.
